title: Trump: Ivanka Trump lies in sworn testimony to DC Attorney General's office
description_short: Trump: Ivanka Trump lies in sworn testimony to DC Attorney General's office
description_medium: AP reports that Ivanka Trump testified under oath for more than five hours in the D.C. attorney general’s civil suit over alleged misuse of inaugural funds. The lawsuit alleged more than $1 million in improper payments to the Trump hotel. The report confirms a deposition, but identifies no false answer or finding of perjury; the transcript or an official finding is needed to support the title’s accusation.
description_long: In December 2020, Ivanka Trump said she had been deposed for more than five hours in a civil lawsuit brought by the District of Columbia attorney general’s office. The suit alleged that Donald Trump’s 2017 inaugural committee misused nonprofit donor funds by making improper payments to the Trump International Hotel in Washington. AP reported that the committee paid more than $1 million to the hotel during inauguration week. Ivanka Trump described the inquiry as wasteful and said the hotel had been told to charge a fair market rate. The supplied report establishes that she gave sworn testimony as part of the case; it does not identify a specific answer shown to be knowingly false, nor report a perjury charge or official finding that she lied. The case concerned alleged misuse of nonprofit funds and hotel payments, not immigration policy. Without the deposition transcript or a court or investigative finding addressing a particular answer, the accusation in the title cannot be treated as established.

preserved_fields.title: Trump: Ivanka Trump lies in sworn testimony to DC Attorney General's office
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump: Ivanka Trump lies in sworn testimony to DC Attorney General's office

notes: The linked AP report was read. It confirms Ivanka Trump was deposed for more than five hours in the D.C. attorney general’s civil suit alleging improper inaugural-committee payments to the Trump hotel. Neither AP’s report nor the supplied case summary identifies a knowingly false answer or official finding of lying/perjury. The transcript or such a finding remains missing.

title: Press Freedom Systematic Destruction Through Legal Intimidation and Media Targeting
description_short: Press Freedom Systematic Destruction Through Legal Intimidation and Media Targeting
description_medium: The Committee to Protect Journalists’ 2024 report documents risks journalists faced from violence, online harassment, subpoenas and litigation, including unsuccessful defamation suits by Trump and his campaign against major outlets. It warns that such cases can burden local newsrooms and sources. The report does not supply the entry’s dated case list or evidence that ordinary reporting was systematically criminalized.
description_long: Donald Trump conducted systematic decade-long campaign to destroy press freedom through legal intimidation, journalist targeting, and media harassment that included hundreds of lawsuits, death threat encouragement, and systematic efforts to criminalize journalism while declaring press 'enemy of the people' in comprehensive attack on First Amendment protections and democratic accountability. The comprehensive press destruction included systematic legal harassment through defamation lawsuits designed to bankrupt media organizations while encouraging supporter violence against journalists through 'enemy of the people' rhetoric that created physical threats and security concerns for reporters covering Trump's activities and democratic governance. The media targeting extended to specific journalist harassment including press credential revocations, security clearance eliminations, and systematic exclusion from government access while creating hostile environment where reporters faced physical threats, legal intimidation, and systematic retaliation for factual coverage of Trump administration activities. Trump's press freedom destruction violated First Amendment protections by systematically using legal system to intimidate journalists while encouraging violence against media through rhetoric designed to delegitimize factual reporting and eliminate independent journalism that provided democratic accountability and government oversight. The journalist intimidation created lasting damage to American press freedom while establishing systematic precedent for government harassment of media through legal warfare, physical intimidation, and systematic access denial that eliminated journalistic independence and democratic transparency. The press freedom elimination established Trump's systematic approach to democratic accountability and government transparency, demonstrating willingness to destroy constitutional protections for journalism while using legal intimidation and violence encouragement to eliminate independent media coverage that exposed government misconduct and provided essential democratic oversight through factual reporting and investigation.
subcategory: Press Freedom Destruction and Journalist Intimidation

title: Trump: Elon Musk's PAC accused of scraping voter data in swing states
description_short: Trump: Elon Musk's PAC accused of scraping voter data in swing states
description_medium: CNBC reported that America PAC ads invited voters in swing states to use a “register to vote” page, but some users were instead asked for personal information and were not directed to a state registration site. The PAC’s privacy policy allowed use of submitted data for other activities or fundraising. Michigan officials said they were reviewing the effort; the report did not establish what data was retained or transferred, or that a law was broken.
description_long: In August 2024, CNBC reported that Elon Musk’s America PAC was collecting voter information through online ads promoting a “register to vote” page in battleground states. The site asked some visitors for details including their address and phone number, then showed a thank-you screen without directing them to a state registration portal. The PAC’s privacy policy said submitted information could be used for other activities or fundraising, and a campaign-finance watchdog said the data could support canvassing and other political work. Michigan’s secretary of state said the office was reviewing the PAC’s activities for possible state-law violations; the article also quoted experts who said they could not identify a law that had clearly been broken. The reporting documents a collection funnel and broad privacy language, not evidence of a confirmed transfer to Trump’s campaign, a specific storage practice, or an unlawful use of the data. The available source does not reproduce America PAC’s registration form or establish what information was ultimately retained, shared or deleted.

preserved_fields.title: Trump: Elon Musk's PAC accused of scraping voter data in swing states
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump: Elon Musk's PAC accused of scraping voter data in swing states

notes: The linked CNBC article was reviewed. It describes web forms seeking voter data, a privacy policy permitting use in other activities or fundraising, and a Michigan review; it reports no finding that a law was broken. The article does not establish retention, transfer, or subsequent use of the data, and the full PAC registration form/privacy notice and applicable rule analysis remain missing.

title: Trump & Melania make billions on ‘meme coin' scam
description_short: Trump & Melania make billions on ‘meme coin' scam
description_medium: The linked timeline says Donald Trump launched the endorsed $TRUMP token on January 17, 2025, and Melania Trump launched $MELANIA two days later. It cites rapid increases in their reported market values, but gives no records of token allocations, sales, proceeds received by the family or investor losses. Those figures alone do not establish billions in realized earnings or fraud.
description_long: Trumpfile’s timeline reports that Donald Trump launched the $TRUMP token on January 17, 2025, and that Melania Trump announced a separate $MELANIA token two days later. It says the reported value of the tokens rose rapidly after their launches and describes $TRUMP as the first Trump-themed token to receive his formal endorsement. The page also contrasts the launches with Trump’s earlier criticism of cryptocurrency. These are claims about token launches and market valuation; they do not show how many tokens Trump, Melania Trump or affiliated companies owned, whether or when those holdings were sold, or what cash proceeds they actually received. The linked timeline supplies no transaction records, verified token-allocation data, investor-loss evidence or finding that either launch was fraudulent. A token’s market value is not the same as income realized by its issuer or owners. The available source therefore supports a concise account of the two launches but not the title’s claims that the family made billions or that the coins were a scam.

preserved_fields.title: Trump & Melania make billions on ‘meme coin' scam
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump & Melania make billions on ‘meme coin' scam

notes: The linked Trumpfile page was read; it reports token launch dates and headline value estimates, but supplies no verified allocation table, family proceeds, wallet-sale records, investor-loss figures or fraud finding. Market valuation does not establish realized income. Those specific records remain missing.

title: Trump: U.S. makes deal to deport Americans to El Salvador terrorist prison
description_short: Trump: U.S. makes deal to deport Americans to El Salvador terrorist prison
description_medium: Reuters reported that El Salvador offered to house people deported from the United States, including what it called “dangerous criminals.” AP later reported that the offer extended to deportees of any nationality and potentially U.S. citizens serving prison sentences. The reports leave the written agreement, receiving facility and transfer authority unclear; they do not establish a deal to send Americans specifically to CECOT.
description_long: During Secretary of State Marco Rubio’s February 2025 visit, El Salvador’s President Nayib Bukele offered to house people deported from the United States in Salvadoran prisons. Reuters described the offer as covering “dangerous criminals” from anywhere in the world; AP later reported that Rubio said it could include deportees of any nationality and violent U.S. citizens already serving sentences. That reporting established a public offer and its stated breadth, but details of the arrangement remained limited. The supplied sources do not show a signed agreement authorizing transfers, identify CECOT as the agreed destination for U.S. citizens, or explain the legal process for moving people from U.S. custody into Salvadoran prisons. The headline’s reference to a deal involving Americans and a particular prison therefore goes beyond the Reuters report. The missing agreement text, facility designation and transfer records are needed to establish what the two governments actually authorized and whether any U.S. citizen was transferred under such an arrangement.

preserved_fields.title: Trump: U.S. makes deal to deport Americans to El Salvador terrorist prison
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump: U.S. makes deal to deport Americans to El Salvador terrorist prison

notes: The linked Reuters report was read and AP reporting was consulted for scope. Reuters documents Bukele’s offer to house deported “dangerous criminals”; AP says Rubio described it as including people of any nationality, potentially U.S. citizens in U.S. custody. The supplied reporting does not identify CECOT as an agreed destination for Americans, provide the agreement text, or establish the legal authority or any transfer.
